last_email.angle: Gratitude: thank one person for something specific and concrete they did this week.

today.body:
After you finish lunch, send a brief note to one new person you met today – just “Hi, enjoyed our chat.”

Floor version (if the day feels rough): after lunch, type “Hi.”

Why it works: a tiny, specific outreach lowers the effort barrier and can start a longer conversation.

Español del día: "¿Cómo está el equipo?" – a short, polite question you can use with an inspector after you log in.

Let me know whether you sent the note and what the reply was – just reply with one word: done, floor or skip.

Note from M: Keep it simple; the goal is just the one line after lunch.

b.advice: Use an implementation‑intention that links the exact cue (the moment you log into your computer) to a concrete, physical action (walk straight to the nearest inspection station) and a brief spoken script. Phrase it as: If I log in at 8:00 am, then I will walk to the first inspector I see and say, “Buenos días, ¿cómo va la línea hoy?” If you’re pressed for time, the fallback cue is simply saying “Buenos días.” The tiny reward is the immediate visual cue of the inspector’s face, which signals you’ve completed the step; note the success with a single check‑mark in a notebook. This cue‑action‑script chain creates a habit stack, making the behavior automatic and low‑effort.

t.lesson: After you log into your computer, walk to the nearest inspector and say, "¿Cómo está el equipo hoy?" (How is the team today?). Then note a check‑mark in your notebook.
